  margin-left: 1em;
}
section.main .content .markdown em {
  font-style: italic;
}
section.main .content .markdown strong {
  font-weight: 700;
}
section.main .content .markdown hr {
  position: relative;
  margin: 1.75rem 0;
  border: 0;
  border-top: 1px solid #808080;
  border-top: 1px solid #999999;
}
section.main .content .markdown abbr {
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  font-weight: bold;
  color: #666666;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}
section.main .content .markdown abbr[title] {
  cursor: help;
  border-bottom: 1px dotted #808080;
}
section.main .content .markdown blockquote {
  padding: .5rem 1rem;
  margin: .8rem 0;
  color: #7a7a7a;
  border-left: .25rem solid #e5e5e5;
}
section.main .content .markdown blockquote :last-child {
  margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
}
@media (min-width: 550px) {
  section.main .content .markdown blockquote {
    padding-right: 5rem;
    padding-left: 1.25rem;
  }
}
section.main .content .markdown img {
  margin: 1rem 0;
  max-width: 100%;
}
section.main .content .markdown table {
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  width: 100%;
  border: 1px solid #e5e5e5;
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
section.main .content .markdown td,
section.main .content .markdown th {
  padding: .25rem .5rem;
  border: 1px solid #e5e5e5;
}
section.main .content .markdown tbody tr:nth-child(odd) td,
section.main .content .markdown tbody tr:nth-child(odd) th {
  background-color: #f7f7f7;
}



section.main .content .markdown pre > code {
  background-color: unset;
}
section.main .content .markdown h3 {
  font-size: 1.2rem;
}

      <div class="title-container">
       <h1 class="page-heading">
        Copy command to system clipboard
       </h1>
      </div>
      <div class="meta">
       <div class="date" title="Wed May 30 2018 19:09:13 +0200">
        May 30, 2018
       </div>
      </div>
     </div>
     <div class="markdown">
      <p>
       In Bash you can copy the previous command to the system clipboard directly from
the command line, and have it be correctly quoted, using
      </p>
      <div class="highlight">
       <pre style="color:#d0d0d0;background-color:#202020;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash">$ <span style="color:#24909d">echo</span> !!:q | xsel --clipboard</code></pre>
      </div>
      <p>
       This is very useful for sharing or embedding complex commands. Consider this
example, with a command that includes quotation marks:
      </p>
      <div class="highlight">
       <pre style="color:#d0d0d0;background-color:#202020;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash">$ <span style="color:#24909d">echo</span> <span style="color:#ed9d13">'foo bar'</span>
foo bar
$ <span style="color:#24909d">echo</span> !!:q | xsel -b
<span style="color:#24909d">echo</span> <span style="color:#ed9d13">'echo '</span><span style="color:#ed9d13">\'</span><span style="color:#ed9d13">'foo bar'</span><span style="color:#ed9d13">\'</span><span style="color:#ed9d13">''</span> | xsel -b
$ xsel -b
<span style="color:#24909d">echo</span> <span style="color:#ed9d13">'foo bar'</span></code></pre>
      </div>
      <p>
       The first command, in its entirety, is the command we’re interested in copying.
In the second command, the
       <code>
        !!
       </code>
       history expansion
       <em>
        event designator
       </em>
       selects
the previously executed command, and the
       <code>
        q
       </code>
       <em>
        modifier
       </em>
       wraps the command in
quotation marks, escaping characters as necessary. Wrapping the command in
quotation marks turns it into a single argument to the second
       <code>
        echo
       </code>
       , which
pipes it into
       <code>
        xsel
       </code>
       ’s standard input. The final command dumps the contents of
the clipboard
       <em>
        selection
       </em>
       :
       <code>
        echo 'foo bar'
       </code>
       , as desired.
      </p>
      <p>
       You might have
       <a title="xclip man page">
        <code>
         xclip(1)
        </code>
       </a>
       instead of
       <a title="xsel man page">
        <code>
         xsel(1)
        </code>
       </a>
       , in
which case you’ll need to pass different options, and on macOS you will
probably want to use
       <code>
        pbcopy(1)
       </code>
       .
      </p>
